Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: World Bank ICR states ATS provides technical platform for BCC to participate in the SADC payment platform linking RTGS systems to facilitate cross-border payments; this indicates cross-border capability exists at least for participating banks via RTGS linkages. Extent/retail reach not evidenced in saved notes.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was a World Bank document about the Democratic Republic of Congo (COD/DRC), an entirely different country from Republic of Congo (COG). Fresh evidence: Congo-Brazzaville is a CEMAC member and participates in GIMACPAY, the regional instant payment system run by GIMAC/BEAC, which has treated domestic and cross-border transactions equally since its July 2020 launch and explicitly lists cross-border as a supported use case, with 49%/43% CAGR growth 2020-2022 (AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023). Raised from 2 (Planned) to 5 (Fully functional).

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: Banque Centrale du Congo (BCC) directly operates ATS (RTGS+ACH) and CSD, and (interim) the retail Switch; World Bank ICR notes NPS Department within BCC for oversight and Law 18/019 strengthening supervision. Direct central bank operation/oversight.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source referred to BCC, the Democratic Republic of Congo's central bank — not applicable to Republic of Congo (COG), which uses the regional central bank BEAC under CEMAC. BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY, acts as settlement agent, and directly operates the RTGS (SYGMA) and ACH (SYSTAC) systems in which Congo participates (AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023; BEAC). Value 5 (Direct Operation) confirmed, but on corrected country-appropriate sourcing.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Digital Code provides for breach notification to the (planned) data protection authority / DPO “without delay”, but no clear mandatory timeline and the authority reportedly not yet established; therefore partial/uncertain practical enforceability for payments.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original DLA Piper source was filed under DRC (c=CD), not the Republic of Congo. Congo's own Law No. 29-2019 (10 October 2019), Article 74, mandates breach notification to the Commission (CPDCP) within 72 hours, and to affected data subjects where risk arises (DataGuidance Guidance Note 2021; Journal Officiel). Raised from 2 (Discretionary) to 3 (Mandatory); note the CPDCP oversight body was still not formally established as of March 2026, so practical enforcement is untested.

Comments: Digital Code Law N°23-010 (13 March 2023) contains general personal data protection provisions (Articles 183+), with broad definition including billing/payment data; applies generally (not payments-specific).

Value 2 confirmed on corrected sourcing.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: World Bank ICR (2024) reports operational performance/volumes for RTGS and ACH (e.g., RTGS transactions and volumes) as part of project reporting; no evidence of regular, public, ongoing BCC payments statistics releases. Ad hoc reporting via donor/IFIs.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was a DRC World Bank ICR, irrelevant to COG. BEAC — the regional regulator/operator responsible for Congo-Brazzaville's payment systems under CEMAC — publishes an annual 'Rapport sur les services de paiement dans la CEMAC' (latest listed 2025, covering 2023) on its public circulars page, and AfricaNenda's SIIPS report independently discloses GIMACPAY volumes/values. Raised from 2 (Ad Hoc) to 3 (Annual).

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2023-2028 adopted July 2023 targets underserved; no evidence located of consumer/low-income representation in payment governance bodies (e.g., switch operator governance). Partial pro-poor orientation via strategy only.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source described a DRC interbank payments platform, wrong country entirely — the cited 'National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2023-2028' referred to is DRC's, not Congo's. Congo-Brazzaville's own National Financial Inclusion Strategy (SNIF) is still in draft, with a third technical-committee review in December 2025 and validation pending as of the search date. Regionally, BEAC's CEMAC Regional Financial Inclusion Strategy (Feb 2025) and GIMAC's founding mandate explicitly target low-income/vulnerable populations, but no evidence of consumer or small-provider board representation in GIMACPAY governance was found. Value 2 (Partial) confirmed on corrected sourcing.
